title: Full document AST: typed block nodes, not raw markdown source strings

comments.author: home
comments.text:
PROBLEM (verified): `markus ast` returns a DIRECTIVE ast, not a document AST. Markdown between directives comes back as opaque raw source:

  {"type":"markdown","source":"# Test headline

A first paragraph.
"}

This blocks Markus from being a shared content IR. Papyrus's Pretext renderer needs block-level structure (paragraphs, headings, lists) to feed its layout solver, which consumes Article.body as string[] of paragraphs. Today it would have to re-parse Markdown in TypeScript, defeating the single-source-of-truth goal.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND PAPYRUS: README already promises 'the renderer turns that meaning into accessible HTML and responsive CSS - or, later, print, EPUB, or email.' Every one of those targets needs the same thing: a complete, typed document tree. This is that tree.

SCOPE:
1. Parse Markdown blocks into typed AST nodes: heading(level,text), paragraph, list(ordered,items), blockquote, code(lang), table, thematic_break, html (if allowed). Inline content may stay as a string initially IF the string is documented as inline-Markdown; prefer typed inline nodes (text/emphasis/strong/link/code) if tractable.
2. Directives keep current shape; they become peers of block nodes in one ordered children[] in document order.
3. Add a schema_version field to the document root. This IR is a contract for downstream consumers; version it from day one.
4. Expose it: keep 'markus ast' output stable/typed, and export a Python API (markusmd.parse_document or similar) returning the same structure.
5. Round-trip integrity: rendering from the AST must produce byte-identical HTML to today's direct render for all examples/ and site/ content. This is the safety net for a maximalist refactor - prove no regression.
6. Behave specs covering each block type + mixed directive/markdown documents.

NON-NEGOTIABLE: no HTML regressions. Existing 'markus convert' output must not change.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
REVIEWED AND ACCEPTED (commit d938d7c, plus fix da1c748).

INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, not taken on report:
- render.py is UNTOUCHED in the diff. That is the strongest possible no-regression evidence: the IR is computed from the same markdown-it token stream purely for serialization, so its existence cannot alter rendered HTML.
- Round-trip: re-ran markus convert across all 4 renderable md files on main vs branch. Byte-identical.
- behave: 158 scenarios / 848 steps passed. ruff: clean.
- IR shape validated against a realistic newsroom article (front matter + pull-quote + card-grid): schema_version present, front matter parsed, typed paragraphs and directives as ordered peers.
- Prototyped the Pretext projection against the real IR: it yields exactly Article.body string[] + pullQuotes string[], with card-grid degrading to inline content and NOTHING dropped. The shared-schema thesis is now proven, not asserted.

DEFECT I FOUND AND FIXED (agent did not report it): the commit downgraded the package version 0.4.0 -> 0.1.0 in BOTH pyproject.toml and src/markusmd/__init__.py. Unintended; would have shipped a version regression. Fixed in da1c748.

DESIGN CALL UPHELD: naming the inline node 'code_span' distinct from block 'code' is correct and should stay. A JSON consumer filtering on type must not have to inspect nesting depth to know which shape it has. Keep it.

SPLIT OUT: kanbus-dacb70 (markus ast crashes on date front matter, pre-existing).

Remaining risk for downstream: the renderable corpus is only 4 files, so round-trip coverage is real but thin. Papyrus content migration (PPY-b794e1) will be the first broad exercise of this IR.
